taskSets.title: Reading source P-A

stimulus.content:
Clothing has changed over time. In ancient societies such as Egypt, Greece and Rome, clothes could show a person’s social position.

During the Industrial Revolution, new manufacturing methods made clothing more widely available. This changed how clothes were produced and bought.

Today, clothes can still express personal choices and cultural traditions. Some designers also think about reducing waste and the environmental effects of making clothes. The history of clothing includes changes in materials, production and people’s choices.

taskSets.title: Reading source P-B

stimulus.content:
Fashion describes trends that are popular at a particular time. Personal style is the way someone chooses to dress. A person may use a trend, adapt it or decide not to follow it.

Ani notices that bright jackets are popular this month. She keeps wearing her plain shirt because it is comfortable and she likes combining it with different trousers. This is one example of a personal choice.

Classic styles use simple designs that remain popular for a long time. Retro styles draw on clothes from an earlier period. Casual clothes are relaxed choices for everyday activities. These labels describe clothing, not the whole person wearing it. An outfit alone cannot tell us someone’s character.

taskSets.title: Reading source P-C

stimulus.content:
Card A — textbook
The textbook describes Coco Chanel as a designer associated with simpler, comfortable clothes. This card gives one example of how a designer can influence clothing.

Card B — Armenian design
Aram Nikolyan is an Armenian designer. His studio is called NIKOLYAN. The Fashion and Design Chamber of Armenia describes his work as drawing on Armenian culture and traditions while creating contemporary clothing. Here, contemporary means belonging to the present time.

Read the cards for information. You do not need to prefer either designer or buy any of their clothes.

taskSets.title: Reading source DA-A

stimulus.content:
For the school magazine, each student must show two looks made with the same main item. Nobody is asked to buy new clothes.

Arpi chooses a plain waistcoat. For the first look, she wears it with a white blouse and formal trousers. For the second, she wears it over a striped T-shirt with jeans.

The magazine prints both pictures side by side. Readers are asked to notice what changes and what stays the same, rather than vote for the most expensive outfit.

taskSets.title: Reading source DA-B

stimulus.content:
This short profile is based on the Fashion and Design Chamber of Armenia. Vahan Khachatryan grew up in Yerevan with paintings by his grandfather around him.

His interest in making clothes began in childhood. He later studied fashion in Florence and graduated in 2011. He founded his own design studio in 2013.

The profile connects his work with the art he grew up with and with cultures he encountered while travelling.

taskSets.title: Reading source MA-A

stimulus.content:
One actor plays two characters in a short school play. Narek, who prepares the costumes, wants the actor to change looks quickly.

He uses the same dark jacket for both characters. For the first character, he adds a large blue collar. For the second, he removes the collar and adds a broad belt.

The jacket stays on throughout the change. The plan changes a few visible details instead of replacing the whole outfit.

taskSets.title: Reading source MA-B

stimulus.content:
This short profile is based on the Fashion and Design Chamber of Armenia. The Armenian fashion brand FAINA began in 2007. Its designer launched a second brand, f by faina, in 2016.

The profile describes clothes that combine simple, elegant shapes with noticeable details. It presents these choices as ways for different wearers to express their own character.

These are facts and descriptions reported by the profile, not a recommendation to prefer or buy the clothes.
